\chapter{Introduction}\label{ch:intro}

\section{Problem statement}

\subsection{The problem}

Getting an AI answer about something on screen is slow and breaks concentration. The usual routine is:

\begin{enumerate}
\item take a screenshot,
\item crop it,
\item open a chatbot website,
\item paste the image,
\item retype the context,
\item wait, then
\item switch back to the original application.
\end{enumerate}

For a student reading a paper, an engineer debugging an error dialog, or anyone comparing two charts, this is seven manual steps for one question.

\subsection{Why this needs a cloud solution}

Putting the AI call directly in a desktop program creates three problems that only a cloud design solves:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Secrets.} Model APIs need keys. A key inside a distributed program can be extracted, and then anyone can spend the owner's money.
\item \textbf{Identity and fairness.} Without a server there is no way to know who is calling or to limit how much each person can use, so one user (or one script) can exhaust the quota for everyone.
\item \textbf{Elasticity and operations.} Model traffic is bursty. A managed, stateless service can scale with demand, and it gives one place to monitor latency and failures.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Scope}

\textbf{In scope.} A Windows desktop application (select a screen region or text, ask, get a streamed answer in a floating panel) and a cloud API that authenticates users, enforces per-user quotas, validates input, routes to an AI model with vision, and streams the answer back.

\textbf{Out of scope.} A mobile or web client, training models, storing conversations or screenshots in the cloud (deliberately excluded for privacy), and billing.

O1 & Shortcut \ensuremath{\rightarrow} selection overlay \ensuremath{\rightarrow} finished crop, fast & Overlay on screen in under 100 ms; crop ready in under 1 s (\S{}8.3) \\
O2 & Mark exactly what to ask about & Rectangle, ellipse, lasso, pen, arrow, highlight and blur tools; several regions per question \\
O3 & Understand text and images & Local OCR plus a vision-capable model; follow-up questions reuse the screenshot \\
O4 & Stream answers into a floating panel & First tokens render as they arrive; stop, retry and copy work \\
O5 & Secure, authenticated cloud API & Every request needs a verified identity; limits and validation enforced \\
O6 & Per-user usage control in the cloud & Quota never exceeded, even under concurrent requests \\
O7 & Privacy by design & No screenshots or prompts stored or logged; the user is told what is sent \\
O8 & Measurable performance & Capture, OCR, upload, first-token and total latency recorded \\
O9 & Lightweight client & Low memory and idle CPU \\
